steps.message:
Checkout felt sluggish about six hours ago - customers noticed. What slowed down, why, and
which piece of the stack was the main bottleneck? Summarize what backs your conclusion, and
include a representative trace id if you find one.

{"status": "concluded", "conclusionStatus": "supported_explanation", "summary": "Checkout became sluggish because the **order-service's database** degraded, starting around 04:13 UTC. The earliest sign was a "database connection timeout" log entry at 04:13, followed by repeated slow-query warnings on the products and sessions tables (569–2511 ms). Order-service average latency rose from ~45 ms baseline to ~160 ms peak (3.5×), with individual POST /api/orders traces reaching 17.6 seconds total, of which 12.7 s was consumed inside order-service. The user-service also logged occasional slow DB queries and 5xx errors but its average latency was declining, making order-service the dominant bottleneck. Payment-service was unaffected.

**What slowed down:** POST /api/orders, GET /api/cart, and GET /api/products — the core checkout flow.

**Why:** Database performance degradation (slow queries + connection timeouts) inside order-service, most likely on the products and sessions tables.

**Main bottleneck:** The **order-service → database** layer. In the slowest representative trace (`4715b7764646608b1a48f1b3a2cec04b`, 17.6 s POST /api/orders), order-service accounted for 12.7 s (72 %) of total duration. A second trace with errors (`0595f4e097fcacc5724644e76d76ad60`) confirmed that the user-service child call took only 25 ms, so the bulk of delay is internal to order-service, consistent with uninstrumented DB wait time.

**Evidence backing this:** (1) Traces showing 5–17 s checkout durations concentrated in 05:09–05:46 UTC with order-service consuming the majority of time. (2) Prometheus range data showing order-service average latency tripling while other services held flat. (3) Order-service logs showing database connection timeouts and slow queries starting at 04:13.
